The brittleness of plasticized cellulose acetate (pCA) remains a major obstacle to its broader application. Although blending with tougher biopolymers is a common approach to mitigate this drawback, the resulting improvement in toughness is often limited due to poor compatibility between the blend constituents. In this work, poly(3-hydroxybutyrate-co-4-hydroxybutyrate) (P34HB), known as amorphous polyhydroxyalkanoate (aPHA), was incorporated into the pCA matrix at three different ratios. Although solubility parameter calculations indicated partial miscibility between the two polymers, glass transition temperature (Tg) and morphological observations confirmed complete immiscibility. To enhance interfacial compatibility, various amounts of a compatibilizer; maleic anhydride (MA)-grafted hybrid blend, and CaCO₃ were introduced into the optimized blend ratio. Morphological analysis revealed a droplet-matrix structure in which the droplet size of the dispersed aPHA  decreased upon the addition of each additive individually, demonstrating their compatibilizing effect. Consequently, the elongation at break, impact strength, and heat deflection temperature increased by up to 63%, 36%, and 12%, respectively, compared to the neat blend after the addition of MA-based compatibilizer. While rheological properties improved slightly, the thermal stability of the neat blend was significantly enhanced, with the onset degradation temperature (Tₒₙₛₑₜ) increasing by up to 21 °C. However, when both additives were combined, no synergistic effect was observed, and the overall performance of the biocomposite declined. These findings suggest that the developed pCA/aPHA-based biocomposite with an optimized amount of the compatibilizer exhibits balanced mechanical and thermal properties, making it a promising candidate for rigid packaging applications.
